summary: Setup is hard for the main path: an app with Gmail scopes can test with up to 100 listed users right away, but opening it to any user requires Google verification of restricted scopes plus an annual third-party security assessment. The main thing that can hold up launch is restricted-scope verification and the CASA assessment, which costs $500 to $4,500 in assessor fees.
effort: 3–5 days of work, plus the security assessment
cost: $500–4,500 USD third-party security assessment fee, paid per assessment (figure quoted on the Google Health API page, which uses the same CASA program)

gates.title: Any Google Account can register the app
Testing mode caps you at 100 test users and 7-day authorizations
gates.what: While the publishing status is Testing, only users listed on the consent screen can authorize, and their authorizations and refresh tokens expire after seven days.
gates.where: Google Cloud console > Google Auth Platform > Audience; the developer adds test users.
gates.todo: Add your own and testers' accounts as test users for development, expect weekly re-authorization, and click Publish app when ready for outside users.

gates.title: Google must verify the app before users can connect without warnings or the 100-user cap
gates.what: Apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes show an unverified-app warning and are capped at 100 total new users until verified. Most Gmail scopes (read, modify, compose, send, metadata) are classed as high-risk by Google Workspace; verification needs brand verification, scope justification and possibly a demo video. Manual brand verification takes 2-3 business days.
gates.where: Google Cloud console > Google Auth Platform > Branding (Verify Branding) and Verification Center (Data access); the developer acts.
gates.todo: Publish the app, verify branding, then request data access verification in the Verification Center and answer Trust & Safety emails.

gates.title: Workspace admins can block or restrict your app for their users
gates.what: A Google Workspace admin can mark the app Trusted, Limited or Blocked, and can restrict Gmail so that users cannot add an app using high-risk Gmail scopes unless the admin trusts it.
gates.where: Google Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Third-Party App Access; the end user's Workspace admin acts.
gates.todo: Publish your OAuth client ID in help docs for Workspace admins so they can trust it, and monitor your support email.

gates.title: No paid plan is required to use the API
Restricted scopes need an annual security assessment
gates.what: Apps with restricted scopes must complete a CASA security assessment every year, and Google's Trust & Safety team notifies the developer with instructions when it is due.
gates.where: Assessment by an authorized third-party assessor; Letter of Validation submitted to Google Trust & Safety. The developer acts.
gates.todo: Plan the yearly assessment and budget, and submit the Letter of Validation when Trust & Safety asks.

requirements.text: A Google Account and a Google Cloud project
A publicly accessible app home page on a domain you own, verified in Google Search Console
A privacy policy hosted on the same domain as the home page that discloses how Google user data is accessed, used, stored and shared
Budget for the CASA security assessment if requesting restricted Gmail scopes

steps.text: Create a Google Cloud project and open Google Auth Platform.
steps.why: The project holds the consent screen and OAuth clients.
steps.detail: Create it inside an organization if you use Google Workspace so ownership is not tied to one person.

steps.why: External makes the app available to any user with a Google Account; Internal limits it to members of your Cloud organization and users outside get an org_internal error. An app for outside users needs External.

steps.text: Fill in the branding fields: app name, logo, support email, home page, privacy policy, authorized domains.
steps.why: These populate the consent screen and are checked in brand verification.
steps.detail: Home page must be public; the privacy policy must be on the same domain. Verify each authorized domain in Google Search Console.

steps.text: Declare the narrowest Gmail scopes your features need under Data Access.
steps.why: Scope classification (non-sensitive, sensitive, restricted) decides which verification applies.

steps.text: Create an OAuth client and add your accounts as test users.
steps.why: Testing status only lets listed test users authorize.
steps.detail: Up to 100 test users; authorizations expire after 7 days.

steps.text: Click Publish app to move the project to In production.
steps.why: Publishing makes the app available to any Google Account; unverified sensitive or restricted scopes then show a warning and the 100-user cap.

steps.text: Click Verify Branding, then Publish branding once it reads Ready to publish.
steps.why: Verifies the name and logo so they appear on the consent screen.
steps.detail: Publish within 7 days of a successful check or the verification has to be re-run.

steps.text: Request data access verification in the Verification Center and provide scope justifications and a demo video if asked.
steps.why: Required for sensitive and restricted scopes before the user cap is lifted.
steps.detail: Branding must be published first. Reply to Trust & Safety emails sent to your developer contact and support email.

steps.text: Wait for Google's verification review and respond to any requests.
steps.detail: Manual branding review takes 2-3 business days.

steps.text: Complete the CASA security assessment with an authorized assessor and submit the Letter of Validation to Trust & Safety.
steps.why: Required for restricted scopes; Trust & Safety tells you when to start.
steps.detail: Fees are paid to the assessor, $500 to $4,500 USD by app complexity.

blockers.problem: Test users get a warning screen and are logged out after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Expect weekly re-authorization in Testing mode, or publish and complete verification.

blockers.problem: Users see the 'unverified app' screen and new sign-ups stop after 100 users.
blockers.fix: Complete verification for all requested scopes; the cap is lifetime and cannot be reset.

blockers.problem: Branding verification result expires before you publish it.
blockers.fix: Click Publish branding within 7 days or run verification again.

blockers.problem: Branding cannot be edited while verification is in progress.
blockers.fix: Click Cancel on the ongoing verification, make changes, then re-submit.

blockers.problem: A customer's Workspace admin restricted Gmail, so their users cannot add the app.
blockers.fix: Give the admin your OAuth client ID so they can mark the app Trusted.

couldNotVerify: Which CASA tier a Gmail app falls under, which determines the 2-3 vs 4-6 week assessment time and the fee.
Which specific Gmail scopes are classed as restricted versus sensitive.

claims.statement: In Testing status, projects are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

claims.statement: Test user authorizations expire seven days after consent, as do refresh tokens.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent.

claims.statement: Manual brand review usually takes 2-3 business days.
claims.sourceTitle: Submit for brand verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: In some cases, where a result cannot be automatically determined, your app may undergo a manual review process that usually takes 2-3 business days .

claims.statement: High-risk Gmail scopes include gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose and gmail.send.
claims.sourceTitle: Control which third-party & internal apps access Google Workspace data | Apps & integrations | Google Workspace Help
claims.note: Listed among Gmail high-risk scopes for admin controls; sensitive vs restricted classification not confirmed from Google page.

claims.statement: Unverified apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes are capped at 100 total users and show a warning.
claims.sourceTitle: OAuth app state overview | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: Additionally, for apps requesting sensitive or restricted scopes, unverified app warnings (Danger UI) will be displayed to users, and a hard cap of 100 total users applies.

claims.statement: Apps using restricted scopes must complete an annual CASA security assessment, with assessor fees of $500 to $4,500.
claims.sourceTitle: App verification | Google Health API | Google for Developers
claims.quote: In addition to OAuth verification, apps using restricted scopes must also complete an annual security assessment based on the Cloud App Security Assessment framework (CASA) .
claims.note: Page is for the Google Health API; applied to Gmail restricted scopes by inference from the shared CASA program and the gate findings. Fee range is on the same page.

claims.statement: Workspace admins can mark apps Trusted, Limited or Blocked.
claims.sourceTitle: Control which third-party & internal apps access Google Workspace data | Apps & integrations | Google Workspace Help

claims.statement: Admins can restrict Gmail so users cannot add an untrusted app requesting a restricted service.
claims.sourceTitle: Control which third-party & internal apps access Google Workspace data | Apps & integrations | Google Workspace Help
claims.quote: While users are prompted to consent to apps, if an app requests access to a restricted service and you haven't specifically trusted the app, users can't add it.

claims.statement: Authorized domains must be verified in Google Search Console and the privacy policy must be on the home page domain.
claims.sourceTitle: Submit for brand verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen of the Google API Console.

claims.statement: No business account or approval is mentioned for registering a Google Cloud OAuth app.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.note: No business account, paid plan or approval requirement is mentioned in Manage App Audience; the console probe required only a Google sign-in.

claims.statement: No paid plan or paid API tier for Gmail API use is mentioned in the pages provided.
claims.sourceTitle: OAuth app state overview | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.note: No paid tier is mentioned in the OAuth app state overview.

claims.statement: External projects are available to any user with a Google Account.
claims.sourceTitle: Manage App Audience - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
claims.quote: Projects configured with a user type of External are available to any user with a Google Account.

claims.statement: Brand verification results are valid for 7 days; data access verification requires published branding.
claims.sourceTitle: Submit for brand verification | App verification to use Google Authorization APIs | Google for Developers
claims.quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.
claims.note: The 7-day validity is stated on the same page in a note.
